name: Easy Bundles
summary: Shopify bundle builder for build-your-own-box, gift-box, mix-and-match, fixed-price, volume and subscription bundles, with bundle inventory synced across Shopify and 3PLs and POS support.
best_for: Shopify merchants who want build-your-own-box, gift-box, mix-and-match, fixed-price or volume bundles live in days rather than sprints, with bundle inventory syncing across Shopify and 3PLs and bundles that also sell through POS, and whose bundle revenue is still small enough to sit comfortably inside a published tier
skip_if: your bundle sales already run past $10,000 a month, because that is where the published ladder ends and the overage is not disclosed; or you need one straightforward fixed or mix-and-match bundle, which Shopify's own free first-party Bundles app already covers
honest_knock: The pricing is tied to the thing the app is supposed to grow. A revenue meter reads as generous at the bottom ($500 of bundle sales a month free is a real trial, not a crippled one) but it means every tier upgrade is triggered by the app working, and the published ladder stops at $10,000 a month with no stated overage. A store doing well on bundles has to ask what comes next rather than read it, and that is the wrong moment to be negotiating. Maturity is not the concern here: the app has been on the App Store since 15 September 2022 and carried 4.9 stars over 1,216 reviews on 4 September 2026 and 1,298 on 19 September, at the same average. The concern is where the money goes as you succeed. Two smaller things: the features most merchants picture when they think bundles are all paid: the guided single- and multi-step build-your-own-box builders sit on Essential at $29, and subscription bundles, add-ons and free gifts on Growth at $49: none of them on the free plan, and the recent reviews that praise the app most warmly also praise the support team by name, which is a compliment to people rather than to a product that never needs them.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Essential · per month, or $299 a year
pricing.notes: (read 2026-09-04 on apps.shopify.com/bundle-builder) Four tiers billed in USD every 30 days, and the meter is the part that matters: you are charged on bundle sales, not on orders, products or staff. The free plan is free to install and covers up to $500 of bundle sales a month. Essential is $29 a month or $299 a year and lifts that to $3,000; Growth is $49 or $499 a year up to $5,000; Scale is $99 or $999 a year up to $10,000. Annual billing saves 14% to 16% depending on the tier, and every paid tier has a 15-day free trial. Features climb the same ladder: free gives mix-and-match, fixed and volume bundles with templates and a custom or template design; Essential adds the single-step and multi-step bundle builders, landing-page templates, search and filtering, and multi-currency and multi-language support; Growth adds advanced discount logic, custom personalisation fields, add-ons, free gifts and subscription bundles; Scale adds AI-generated designs, advanced analytics, one-to-one onboarding and an account manager on Slack. Two things the block does not say are worth noting before you commit. It does not publish what happens when you pass $10,000 of bundle sales in a month, and it does not publish an overage rate; the plan table simply ends there and links out to see all pricing options. On a re-read of the same listing on 3 November 2026 every amount above was unchanged, and the free and Essential cards now add one line each: "Not applicable for Shopify Plus and Advanced plans." Growth and Scale carry no such line, so a store on Shopify Plus or Advanced should budget from Growth.

compare_with.name: Shopify's own Bundles app
compare_with.why: Shopify ships a free, first-party bundles app that handles fixed and mix-and-match bundles with no meter on your revenue, and for a store that wants one simple bundle that is the cheaper answer and always will be. Easy Bundles is worth the $29 to $99 when the bundle is an experience rather than a SKU: a guided build-your-own-box or gift-box flow, subscription bundles, add-ons and free gifts, bundle landing pages in several currencies and languages, and when you want the bundle stock to stay in step with your 3PL without anyone reconciling it by hand

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Easy Bundles, called EB | Easy Bundle Builder in the admin, on a Shopify development store: the install, one mix and match bundle made with the AI assistant (seen only in the editor), the partner plan page that is free on development stores, the table of ten revenue bands for live stores, and the uninstall dialog, after which the app was uninstalled. Nothing was paid and no theme change was made. Install: the App Store listing is Easy Bundles, apps.shopify.com/bundle-builder, by Skai Lama; in the admin the app is called EB | Easy Bundle Builder. The install click was at 15:40:44 and the app was open in the admin at 15:41:10, about 30 seconds later. The Install app dialog asked for View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data. A welcome screen Every way to bundle, in one app with a Continue button led straight to the plan page. No vendor account, call, demo or phone number was asked. Another bundle app (Fast Bundle) was already installed in the store; only screens of the EB app were used. Core action, a mix and match bundle (build your own box): at 15:42:30 Create with AI was pressed for Mix & match bundle with the prompt Build-your-own gift box: pick any 3 snowboards and save 15%, then Choose Collections, the Automated Collection (8 products) and Select. After about 1.5 minutes of building (about 15:44) the Bundle Editor opened with Build Your Snowboard Gift Box, status Unlisted. The assistant Breezy described one step Pick Your Snowboards with the Automated Collection of 8 snowboards, the rule Shopper must pick exactly 3 snowboards to continue and Discount: 15% off when they have 3 items, with no upsell offer yet; the preview said Add 3 product(s) to save 15%! The core action took 7 steps (4 clicks in the choice, the prompt, the collection and Select), followed by a waiting screen Building your bundle. The store has a password (a notice said that the online store is password protected), so Safe mode (a sample page) was chosen. The editor also said App extension off - Bundle can't display with a Turn on button; we did not press it and made no theme change. Clicking Add to Bundle in the editor only selected the element (edit mode), so the shopper side (picking 3 products and the 15% discount in the cart) was not seen. A chat bubble of the vendor with a message from a vendor staff member (I'm 80% sure this bundle is great, the other 20% is why a human is sitting right here) appeared in the editor; we did not answer it. Plans: the plan page is called Your partner plan and says No plan picker, no revenue bands. Partner and development stores get everything, free. Free on this store, always, with the button Start free as a partner (pressed, it costs nothing), No card, no trial clock. No Shopify approval screen followed and no card was asked. The partner plan lists every bundle type (Mix & Match, Pre-curated, Quantity Breaks), no bundle revenue limits, a shared Slack channel with the bundles team and Bundle Studio early access; there is also a partner program with a 20% revenue share. The section What your clients will pay lists the prices for live stores by monthly bundle revenue: Starter under $500 Free; Essential $500 to $3,000 $29 a month; Growth $3,000 to $5,000 $49; Scale $5,000 to $10,000 $99; Pro $10,000 to $20,000 $149; Advanced $20,000 to $30,000 $199; Elite $30,000 to $50,000 $299; Premier $50,000 to $150,000 $399; Enterprise $150,000 to $500,000 $599; Enterprise Plus $500,000 and above Let's talk. The text says that if bundle revenue passes the limit of the plan, a usage charge tops the store up to the price of the plan that covers it (a Growth store doing $25,000 pays $199 that month either way), and that Shopify asks the store to approve a monthly spending cap before any usage charge applies and that it is never billed above it. Differences from the dossier and the listing: the listing and dossier show four plans (Free, $29, $49 and $99, a 15-day trial, up to $10,000 of bundle revenue); the app shows ten revenue bands up to $500,000 and above and no trial on this store (No card, no trial clock). The overage that the dossier said was not named is described in the app as a top up to the price of the covering band. The spending cap and any usage charge were not seen, because no Shopify approval screen was reached. Cancelling: no subscription ran, so there was nothing to cancel. Removing the app goes through Settings, Apps, the menu of the app and Uninstall; the dialog Uninstall EB | Easy Bundle Builder? says you will no longer be able to use the app, that any data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted, and that a request goes to the app developer within 48 hours to delete all personal customer information. A reason is required and Testing multiple apps was chosen. The message You've successfully uninstalled EB | Easy Bundle Builder appeared at about 15:52. Not tested: the bundle in the real storefront (the app extension was off and the store has a password), the cart and checkout, subscription bundles, the paid plans and any usage charge, the Slack channel and the 1:1 onboarding. Clean up: the app was uninstalled at about 15:52 and the installed list no longer showed it; other apps were not touched; no theme change was made; all our own browser tabs were closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The bundle was seen only in the editor because the app extension was off and the store has a password, the plan page for a development store shows no prices and the real prices sit in a closed section, the app shows ten revenue bands where the dossier shows four plans, a usage charge tops a store up to the price of the covering band, a chat bubble of the vendor appeared in the editor, and the app has a different name in the admin and in the App Store.
